title: Protect ZIP entry contents with a supported password algorithm
goal: Create and read password-protected ZIP entries with explicit algorithm selection, failure handling and compatibility limits.

selectionNotes: Create and read password-protected ZIP entries with explicit algorithm selection, failure handling and compatibility limits. Desktop/server examples; inspect complete constraints before use.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses or relies on .NET 11 framework APIs/behaviour; .NET 10 is comparison-only.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 comparison with its matching SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical .NET 11 project selects its supported C# 15 default.

platforms: Desktop/server .NET platforms; authoring execution recorded on Windows. Browser/WASI excluded from these samples.
prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0, implicit usings and the namespaces stated in the complete recipe. No additional package, workload, account or provider is required.
constraints: WinZip AES-128/192/256 and legacy ZipCrypto round-trip in this baseline. Prefer AES-256; ZipCrypto is weak and suitable only for deliberate legacy interoperability. Password entropy still matters; ZIP passwords are not account authentication, a key vault or a substitute for a reviewed secure-transfer design. Entry names and archive metadata remain visible. An empty password for an encrypted entry throws ArgumentException; a wrong password throws InvalidDataException in the tested cases. Unknown encryption is unsupported and must not be silently downgraded. Read to EOF before accepting plaintext because authentication/integrity can fail late. Do not log passwords; the caller supplies them at runtime. Strings cannot be reliably erased. Browser/WASI AES support is unavailable; this desktop/server example excludes both. Directory extraction can leave partial output on failure or cancellation: use a fresh staging directory, accept only after complete success, and clean failures. OverwriteFiles=false rejects existing files; it does not make extraction atomic. No interoperation with a particular external archive application is claimed.
stabilityLimitations: Verified with SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105; RC2 execution is not GA verification.

sources.title: Official archive integrity, access and encryption implementation

evidence.scope: Actual .NET 10 Windows compilation/execution: plain ZIP access/replacement, stored-CRC and TAR-header corruption acceptance baseline, four TAR formats and raw sparse body. Encryption is explicitly unavailable and its stub is tested. No mocks, cross-compilation or GA proof.

All four algorithms restored the original payload; wrong and missing passwords failed. Actual asynchronous AES-256 directory creation/extraction, overwrite refusal and cancelled extraction were executed. Actual Windows compilation/execution; no mocks, cross-compilation or GA proof.

humanProof.scope: Bounded desktop/server archive and codec checks run locally without external providers or UI. No extra native/device or external-tool interoperability claim.
